label: copy-phase input z (fed-back z) at early-middle recall positions 2-4
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is z, i.e. the model just output z (orig(recall_idx-1) == z). It never fires on z during the original phase or at the delimiter, nor on any other input token. Strongest when z is the 2nd original token (recall_idx 2, ~56% of mass, top activations all like a z ... <DEL> a [z]), still strong at recall_idx 3, weaker at 4, and near-zero at recall_idx 1 and >= 5 or on the final copy step (to_go 0). Magnitude also falls with recall position; z at original position 0 echoed at recall_idx 1 barely fires. False positives are mostly z echoes at recall_idx 3-4 that happen to stay inactive.

issues: Main claims check out on dev: 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase, there is zero activation in the original phase or at the delimiter, in_tok is z for 100% of active steps, and mass by recall_idx is 2=56.4%, 3=37.5%, 4=5.7%, with 1 and >=5 each about 0.1%. Test scores reproduce: P 0.890, R 0.966, F1 0.926, mass recall 0.996.

The false-positive description is somewhat wrong. Within the predicate, recall_idx 3 fires almost every time when L>=5 (precision 0.97 to 1.0). The false positives come from two places. First, recall_idx 4: about 40% precision at L=6, where to_go=1, and about 75-80% at L>=7. Second, recall_idx 2 at L=4, where to_go=1: 63% precision. So most false positives sit at recall_idx 4 and at to_go=1 in short sequences, not spread over recall_idx 3-4.

At recall_idx 4 with L>=7, the feature stays off about 25% of the time. I found no simple variable that explains it: in_count, a digit next_out, n_digits, first_tok and correct (always 1) all leave precision at 0.73-0.84. This looks like graded dependence on hidden state rather than a clean subclass.
Small residual: at L=9 the feature also fires weakly at recall_idx 1 (about 11%) and recall_idx 5 (about 14%). This is negligible in mass.

Alternative predicates gain little. Requiring to_go>=2 only at recall_idx 4 gives test F1 0.932 (P 0.926, R 0.937). Requiring to_go>=2 everywhere gives 0.881. An L-gated window gives 0.921. The original predicate is essentially as good as these.
